Consider the triangle $△ABC$ shown above. The line segment $\overset{―}{CH}$ is the altitude corresponding to $\overset{―}{AB}.$ If $m∠BAC={120}^{∘},$ calculate $m∠HCA.$
questions.worked_solution:
Since the straight angle must have a measure of ${180}^{∘},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠HAC+m∠BAC & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠HAC+{120}^{∘} & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠HAC & ={60}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $△AHC$ is a right triangle. Since its interior angles must sum to ${180}^{∘},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠HCA+m∠HAC+m∠AHC & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠HCA+{60}^{∘}+{90}^{∘} & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠HCA+{150}^{∘} & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠HCA & ={30}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Example: 
                    Calculating an Unknown Angle
canonical_examples.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14187003/assets/33700b49845ba054447ce69356324d3e421d256344149b447756cdbf0cf5a905.png)

Consider $\triangle ABC$ shown above. The line segment $\overline{CH}$ is the altitude corresponding to $\overline{AB}.$ If $m\angle BAC = 115^\circ,$ calculate $m\angle HCA.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Since the straight angle must have a measure of $180^\circ,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠HAC+m∠BAC & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠HAC+{115}^{∘} & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠HAC & ={65}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $\triangle ACH$ is a right triangle. Since its interior angles must sum to $180^\circ,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠HCA+m∠HAC+m∠AHC & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠HCA+{65}^{∘}+{90}^{∘} & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠HCA+{155}^{∘} & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠HCA & ={25}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

tutorials.name: Introduction
tutorials.problem:
Consider $\triangle ABC$ shown below. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14187003/assets/6fdb9a8337d16f1ef1910989b3df92844c5393c33108f98ae7993cc939bed0b3.png)

Now, let's draw a line segment that 

- runs from $\color{blue}C$ to the line ${\color{red}\overset{\longleftrightarrow}{AB}},$ and

- is *perpendicular* to ${\color{red}\overset{\longleftrightarrow}{AB}}.$

This line segment is the dashed segment shown below:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14187003/assets/4a7ee2771c9b0c60dbb07c43b0439e822ea9b2c261ac41af9b44fec72b9f2a91.png)

Finally, let's label the other endpoint of our segment ${\color{blue}{H}}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14187003/assets/758eab533719220515460b6677054438a9ac0e2701d1a5267b973e526f63bd90.png)

Note the following:

- The line segment ${\color{blue}\overline{CH}}$ is called the **height** (or **altitude**) *corresponding to* ${\color{red}\overset{\longleftrightarrow}{AB}}.$

- The line $\overset{\longleftrightarrow}{AB}$ is called the **base** of the altitude ${\color{blue}\overline{CH}}.$

As we'll soon discover, the heights and their corresponding bases are important attributes of triangles.

tutorials.name: Case of Extended Bases
tutorials.problem:
We can draw exactly three heights (or altitudes) in any triangle. However, sometimes the height lies outside the triangle.

To demonstrate, consider $\triangle{ABC}$ below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14187003/assets/df1ac2c1074305f8ead506d9aeb8c3927ad51ae5949b45976f1971b52d402ee5.png)

The height corresponding to $\overline{BC}$ is a line segment that 

- runs from the opposite vertex $A$ to the line $\overset{\longleftrightarrow}{BC},$ and

- is perpendicular to $\overset{\longleftrightarrow}{BC}.$

In this case, it's impossible to draw a perpendicular from $A$ to the *segment* $\overline{BC}.$ However, we can first *extend* the line segment $\overline{BC}$ as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14187003/assets/26bf9eb8af1e9b71c263c08cae5797d5c911410985cdc01213ac2c295f7b8d46.png)

Now, we draw the perpendicular from $A$ to $\overset{\longleftrightarrow}{BC}.$ This gives the height $\overline{AH}{:}$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14187003/assets/894686fce1393ebcf998be6885020627c9f3cde5916adfec67234f15f8895826.png)
